proof_contract: For stationary Gaussian AR(1), write independent standard normals Z0=X0/sqrt(gamma0), Zt=epsilon_t/sigma. The score S=sum X_(t-1) epsilon_t is Z-prime K_T Z, where diagonal K=0, K_(0,t)=sigma sqrt(gamma0) phi^(t-1)/2 and K_(j,t)=sigma^2 phi^(t-j-1)/2 for 1<=j<t. Each absolute row sum is bounded uniformly in T by max{sigma sqrt(gamma0)/(2(1-|phi|)), sigma sqrt(gamma0)/2+sigma^2/(1-|phi|)}. The symmetric spectral theorem and orthogonal Gaussian invariance yield independent centered terms lambda_j(Z_j^2-1), with 2 sum lambda_j^2=Var S=T gamma0 sigma^2 and max|lambda_j| bounded. Divide by sqrt(T gamma0 sigma^2): total variance1 and sum absolute third moments tends to0 because E|Z^2-1|^3<=E(Z^2+1)^3=28 and max normalized weight is O(T^-1/2). Extend the already proved v03-c06 smooth Lindeberg replacement to this row of independent unequal-variance terms: the third-order Taylor remainder sum vanishes; their independent Gaussian replacements sum exactly to N(0,1); the same smooth-CDF squeeze completes the proof. No unproved Levy theorem or conditional normality given the full lagged design is needed. Combine the covariance-square LLN for Sxx/T, score expansion and residual-variance consistency for the stable OLS limit and feasible studentization. State fixed |phi|<1 and stationary Gaussian initialization independent of future shocks.

Prove the special Gaussian unit-root slope and conventional-statistic limits via Brownian-grid equality in law, pathwise Riemann sums, L2 quadratic variation, positive denominator and residual variance consistency. Preserve zero initial level/no deterministic terms and distinguish fixed stationary from unit-root inference.

For finite-order ARMA define causal, invertible, innovations/information and cancellations. Prove the explicit ARMA(1,1) filter/recovery/covariance/forecast formulas. If giving a general root theorem, supply the repeated-root power-series proof or clearly mark it as a scoped invoked result with actual evidence. A simpler sufficient matrix-power bound is acceptable for VAR(p) companion discussion.

Prove the geometric VAR covariance series, Lyapunov existence/uniqueness, known-parameter forecasts and exact Gaussian covariance-factor nonidentification. Discuss estimation/Granger inference only under explicitly stated extra laws; do not copy the source LR/vec errors.

Explicit common-trend plus stationary-spread system: prove cointegration, error-correction identity and uniqueness, conditional covariance, T rate and known-parameter forecasts. Avoid zero-initial-spread/stationary-covariance conflation. If adding a mixed-normal OLS limit, restrict to independently generated white Gaussian spread and prove its conditional-law mixture.

GARCH positive product-series sufficient strict stationarity with E|log A| finite and E log A<0; independently derive second and fourth moment conditions, relevant uniqueness scope, squared-process covariance when finite, and multistep variance tower. Include both finite-variance/infinite-fourth and strict-stationarity/infinite-variance transfers. Do not assert QMLE inference as proved.

Forecast evaluation: fully derive overlapping Gaussian loss and loss-difference covariance, exact fixed-forecast inference, target/probability-law distinction and evaluation-set selection versus independent new-block expected loss. Covariance stationarity alone supplies neither CLT nor HAC consistency.

original_cases.title: Stable ARMA forecasting and invertible shock recovery
original_cases.proof_route: Mean-square convergence from square-summable filter coefficients, exact covariance/tower forecasts under known coefficients and recoverable innovations. General causal ARMA uses cancellation plus root/power-series conditions stated explicitly. Gaussian covariance equivalence identifies the whole zero-mean process law, not a physical shock. Inversion |theta|<1 is a separate past-recovery condition.

original_cases.title: Stable VAR prediction versus structural shock identification
original_cases.proof_route: An explicit geometric matrix-power bound yields the mean-square stationary sum and forecast covariance. Lyapunov uniqueness follows by iterating the homogeneous difference until A powers vanish. Equal Gaussian reduced-form shock covariance under an orthogonal rotation yields observational equivalence, so causal labels need additional restrictions.

original_cases.title: Stable coefficient inference versus the Gaussian unit-root limit
original_cases.proof_route: For stationary Gaussian AR1, prove Sxx/T convergence from Cov(X_i^2,X_j^2)=2 gamma(i-j)^2, score LLN from martingale orthogonality. For normality, use a fully explained Gaussian quadratic-form eigenvalue/characteristic-function proof with bounded eigenvalues and variance T gamma0 sigma2, or an explicitly proved appropriate CLT; do not infer conditional normality by conditioning on the full lagged design. For the zero-start Gaussian random walk, exact Brownian-grid equality in law, path-continuity Riemann sums and L2 quadratic variation prove T(rhohat-1) -> (W(1)^2-1)/(2 integral W^2) and t -> (W(1)^2-1)/(2 sqrt(integral W^2)). Prove residual variance consistency and positive limiting denominator. Drift/intercept, augmented regressions, local-to-unity and general innovations require their own limit laws.

original_cases.title: A common stochastic trend and stationary error correction

inputs.spread_initialization: Stationary N(0,1), independent of all random-walk innovations and future spread innovations; no conditioning on a fixed zero initial spread in the covariance calculation.

original_cases.proof_route: Independent iid Gaussian random-walk innovations and a stationary independent AR1 spread give unique cointegrating slope: any other slope leaves variance growing linearly. Derive the exact error-correction identity, then known-parameter forecasts. Conditional on the observed x vector, the slope error is centered Gaussian with x prime Omega_v x/(x prime x)^2; serial spread covariance matters. A summable spread covariance/operator bound plus the Brownian denominator proves T-consistency in probability. If proving a mixed-normal level-OLS limit, restrict to independent white spread and show conditional Gaussian mixing explicitly. Estimated residual unit-root tests cannot reuse the known-spread critical law. In the four-date synthetic trajectory recover only innovations at t=2,3,4. Without a recorded v0 the first innovation is not determined. The displayed conditional slope covariance conditions only on the x path and averages over the stationary spread initialization.

original_cases.title: GARCH persistence, moment existence and volatility forecasts
original_cases.proof_route: For positive iid multipliers A and integrable log A with E log A<0, SLLN gives convergent positive past product series and a causal strictly stationary solution. Show the variance moment via Tonelli and the fourth moment under E A^2<1, with independence of current z and past variance. Strict stationarity does not imply finite second moments. Known Gaussian conditional shocks need not yield Gaussian multistep aggregate returns. Squared-process ARMA is a covariance representation only when its moments exist. No universal quasi-likelihood or heavy-tail limit theorem is inherited.

original_cases.title: Overlapping forecast losses and evaluation-set selection
original_cases.proof_route: Future two-step errors sum adjacent iid Gaussian innovations. Expand Gaussian fourth moments to get Cov(e_i^2,e_j^2)=2 Cov(e_i,e_j)^2. For prespecified c the loss difference c^2-2c e_t is Gaussian with an exact finite covariance-sum variance, not iid row variance. Choosing c=mean(e) on the evaluation block instead gives average loss difference -mean(e)^2 and false improvement; an independent future block with disjoint innovations has expected degradation E c^2. Covariance stationarity alone is not a CLT.
